# FrontierAgent skills, plugins, and workflows

> Curated directory of FrontierAgent projects. The curated page is organised by what each FrontierAgent project does for the reader; the generated catalog is the full resolvable set.

This repository ships a curated page for people and generated layers for machines. Everything under
"Generated data" is rewritten in full by the `refresh-catalog` workflow, Mondays at 08:00 UTC and
on manual dispatch, from live sources rather than a committed snapshot. Editing those files by hand
is pointless; they are overwritten.

## Files

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-frontieragent/main/README.md): the curated page, grouped by what each FrontierAgent project does for the reader.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-frontieragent/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the bar an entry has to clear and the exact format a new entry uses.

## Generated data

- [CATALOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-frontieragent/main/CATALOG.md): every FrontierAgent project this repo can resolve and check, as a markdown table. It covers GitHub repositories only. The curated page also lists things that are not repositories, such as the tech report, the model collection, the API platform, the community server, and individual documentation pages inside the upstream repository. Those carry no row here, so this file is a subset of the curated page rather than a superset of it.
- [catalog.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-frontieragent/main/catalog.csv): the same rows as CSV. Header: `name,description,stars,verified,repo_url,screenshots`. Read the header row; do not assume a column order. `screenshots` is semicolon separated and may be empty.
- [plugins.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-frontieragent/main/plugins.json): the same rows as JSON, in the dsh-market registry schema, so a marketplace client can consume this file directly as a registry. Top level: `name, url, source, updated, count, categories, plugins`. Per entry: `name, owner, url, category, description.en, stars, install, added`, plus `npm` and `screenshots` where they exist. The live entry count is the top level `count` field and the as-of date is `updated`, which is why neither is restated anywhere in this file.
- [.github/data/first-seen.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZeroPointRepo/awesome-frontieragent/main/.github/data/first-seen.json): the date this list first carried each entry. Cumulative and never back-dated, so a re-listed entry keeps its original date. It records when the list first carried something, not when that thing was created.

## What the verified mark means

- `✅` in CATALOG.md and `verified: true` in the CSV mean one specific thing: on the last run the repo resolved through the GitHub API, was not archived, was not a fork, and was not a rename of the slug listed here.
- `—` and `verified: false` mean that check did not pass or does not apply. Neither is a claim that the entry is broken.
- The check catches what a link checker structurally cannot see: a renamed repo and an archived repo. Both still return HTTP 200.
- `npm` is present on an entry only when that package exists and its own `repository` field points back at the repo listed here. A looser match would hang someone else's download count on this entry, so the field is absent rather than guessed.
- If more than 5% of README reads fail in a run, the generator keeps the existing catalog rather than publish false unverified marks. It prints every drop and refuses to shrink the set silently. A stale catalog is preferred over a wrong one.
- This is a curated list, not a security audit. A verified mark says the entry resolves, not that its code has been reviewed.

## How an agent should use this list

1. For the complete machine-readable set in one request, fetch `plugins.json`. For tabular work or citation, fetch `catalog.csv`. Both are single files and neither is paginated.
2. For a recommendation to a person, read `README.md`. It is the only layer where entries are curated rather than merely resolvable.
3. Report the `updated` field from `plugins.json` as the as-of date alongside any claim taken from here.
4. Take install commands verbatim from the `install` field or the fenced block. Do not rebuild one from a repository URL, and do not drop or invent a version pin.
5. Carry the verified mark through to the person. Do not present `verified: false` as broken, and do not present `verified: true` as a safety endorsement.
6. Ask the person before installing anything or handing it credentials. Do not invent credentials, endpoints, licences or author attribution.
7. To add or correct an entry, open a pull request against `README.md`. The generated layers are rebuilt from it, so a change made in them is discarded. There is no write API and nothing here accepts a direct push.
